notes: Flat-table shape ready for a relational store — each row in `navigations[]` is one grantable access.
`navigation_id` is the immutable primary key. Users record which IDs they've been granted (see `samples.user_access`).
`catalog_id` is the position of the row inside its `catalog` group (1-based). Useful for stable ordering when rendering.
`sub_navigation = "all-access"` means the main navigation has no fine-grained sub-actions — checking that one row grants the whole page.
When a `main_navigation` has multiple rows (e.g. User Management), each `sub_navigation` is an independent grantable action.
A main navigation's menu is IMPLICITLY visible in the sidebar when the user holds ANY row that belongs to it.
Adding a new row: append to `navigations[]` with a fresh `navigation_id` (never reuse), then bump `template_version`.
Deprecating: set `"deprecated": true` on the row — keep it so existing user grants stay decodable, but hide it in new admin UIs.
Keys are case-insensitive on the wire but stored lowercase in this template for consistency.

columns.catalog_id: int, position within the catalog group (ordering)
columns.catalog: string, top-level bucket the row belongs to
columns.sub_navigation: string, the specific action (or "all-access" for whole-module toggles)
columns.route: optional, Vue Router path the navigation opens
columns.deprecated: optional boolean, hides the row in new UIs but keeps grants decodable

adding_a_new_menu.when: App adds a Loyalty Program page.
adding_a_new_menu.how: Append { "navigation_id": 18, "catalog_id": 9, "catalog": "administrative", "main_navigation": "loyalty program", "sub_navigation": "all-access", "route": "/loyalty" } and bump template_version. Existing users don't need a migration — they simply won't have ID 18 until an admin grants it.
adding_a_new_menu.note: Backend should return the full template on GET /access-template so the admin UI can render new rows without a front-end release.

adding_a_new_sub_action.when: User Management adds a Bulk Import action.
adding_a_new_sub_action.how: Append { "navigation_id": 19, "catalog_id": 7, "catalog": "administrative", "main_navigation": "user management", "sub_navigation": "bulk import", "route": "/users" }. Because the sidebar visibility rule fires when ANY user-management row is present, existing user-management admins keep their menu without needing an update to their granted list.
adding_a_new_sub_action.note: Shift the catalog_id of subscription/store settings +1 if you want to keep dense ordering, or just leave gaps — either works because catalog_id is a display hint, not a key.

deprecating_an_item.when: Reports gets replaced by an analytics module.
deprecating_an_item.how: Mark the row `"deprecated": true`. Admin UIs should hide it by default; the backend keeps interpreting the ID so historical grants still resolve. Only after a clean-up migration on every user should the row be physically deleted.
deprecating_an_item.note: Never re-use a deprecated navigation_id — pick the next unused integer.
